newsitem.title: FINLAND: OKOBANK SAYS TRYGG-HANSA RULING UPHELD.
newsitem.headline: OKOBANK SAYS TRYGG-HANSA RULING UPHELD.

text.p: HELSINKI, Dec 20 - Finnish banking group OKOBANK said on Friday a Swedish appeals court had upheld a lower-court decision in favour of Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa in a 60 million markka dispute between the two companies.
"The court of appeals upheld the lower court's decision in favour of Trygg-Hansa," OKOBANK (Osuuspankkien Keskuspankki Oy) said in a statement.
The bank said the lower court's decision had prompted it to make a credit loss provision in its 1995 accounts, and so the appeals court ruling would have no impact on its 1996 profit.

OKOBANK said the dispute with Trygg-Hansa was over credit insurance issued by Trygg-Hansa and which had secured about 60 million markka in receivables from the Swedish Reinhold group to the bank's Swedish subsidiary, Okobank Sverige.
OKOBANK said it had claimed payment in 1991 because of Reinhold's insolvency, but that Trygg-Hansa had disputed the claim.
A Stockholm court ruled in favour of Trygg-Hansa in 1995, OKOBANK said. The bank said it would consider appealing further to Sweden's supreme court.
